  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 834 0573 9376, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 27, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:05 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  ALERT SOUTH BAY PRESENTATION

Assistant City Manager Davis presented the Silver Award received by Alert South Bay from
the Emergency Services Association - Southern Chapter for the development of integrated
alert and warning innovation enhancements in emergency management, and presented the
latest public service announcement video for Alert South Bay. She then introduced Regional
Emergency Communications Manager Soraya Sutherlin who provided an update on the
Alert South Bay system.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered
under New Business.)

A.  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENTS FOR THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER
  DESIGN AND ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 27, 2021
 Assistant City Manager Davis and Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba
provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved to:

  APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ROESLING
  NAKAMURA TERADA ARCHITECTS, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $234,895
  FOR PROJECT PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS AND A TASK ORDER WITH
  MBI, UNDER THEIR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT, TO
  CONDUCT AN INITIAL STUDY AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION
  (IS/MND) IN THE AMOUNT OF $67,535, SUBJECT TO CITY ATTORNEY
  FINAL REVIEW AND APPROVAL AS TO FORM.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that a number of the public comments received express
concerns regarding traffic and parking. Director Wahba explained both traffic and parking
would be looked at through the IS/MND process.

Environmental Planner, John Bellas of Michael Baker International provided a summary of
the IS/MND process and environmental analysis.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA highlighted the public comments received by the City that
were concerned about the environmental impact analysis (CEQA) occurring before the uses
of the facility have been established. Mr. Bellas explained the reasoning behind the order of
analysis that will take place, noting that a range of analysis can be provided to the Council
for their consideration. City Attorney Davis noted that CEQA is required before the Council
takes any discretionary action.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN expressed concern about proceeding too far into the project, then
having to revise certain elements once the facility uses are established. Director Wahba
stated that it is unlikely that significant changes will need to be made as a result of the
environmental analysis.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested moving ahead with the project, while ensuring that
residents’ concerns regarding traffic and parking will be addressed further along in the process
at the appropriate time.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN expressed concern that architectural changes such as building size
may need to be made due to potential traffic impacts or parking issues discovered further along
in the process.

Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the Professional Services Agreement provides a 30%
deliverable.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF summarized the successful use of the Nature Center in the past
for students who visit the Nature Center via bus which will likely continue, and noted that the
real question is whether or not the Council will approve additional special events such as
weddings and special events, which will have traffic and parking impacts.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF that we should not
be looking to change the project at this time, but should be looking at the impacts of various
types of uses for the facility in the future, which will be presented to the Council by MBI as a
result of the analysis. He stated he was not concerned about parking, and expressed his
excitement for our City to have a state-of-the-art building that will benefit our community and
provide more learning opportunities for our youth. He also noted the potential opportunity for
using the facility as a meeting space for the City’s Homeowner’s Associations.

Discussion ensued regarding analysis of parking demands as it relates to the design versus
the size and scale of various events.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Written public testimony was received as late correspondence by John Rohrer, Paul Moilanen,
Carol Boots Magee and Jennifer Whynaucht.

  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  FOR PROJECT PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS AND A TASK ORDER WITH
  MBI, UNDER THEIR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT, TO
  CONDUCT AN INITIAL STUDY AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION
  (IS/MND) IN THE AMOUNT OF $67,535, SUBJECT TO CITY ATTORNEY
  FINAL REVIEW AND APPROVAL AS TO FORM.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

 City Manager Grammer reported that on July 17, Los Angeles County revised the Health
 Officer Order to require masking for all indoor public settings regardless of vaccination
 status. He reported on the recent increase in transmission rate due to the Delta variant,
 and reported that the CDC announced today updated guidelines urging people to wear
 masks in indoor settings in areas where there are high or substantial transmission levels.
 In RHE, current vaccination rates are 96% for ages 65 and older, 81.5% for ages 16 -64,
 and 62% for youth ages 12-17. Case numbers in RHE have increased over the past two
 weeks with 24 new cases. Outdoor City events are moving ahead as planned, including
 Summer Movie Nights, the Hills Are Alive Race on August 7, City Celebration on
 September 25, the Tracy Austin Tournament planned for late October or early November,
 and the Peninsula Prepared Expo planned as an outdoor event in October.

 MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reported on a letter he drafted, signed by several local
 Mayors and Council Members, written to Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn
 appealing for the local South Bay communities to be exempt from the recent County Health
 Order’s mask mandate based on high vaccination rates and low COVID case numbers.

 City Manager Grammer stated that there is an additional letter that Rancho Palos Verdes,
 Rolling Hills and Palos Verdes Estates are considering, asking the County to rescind the
 recent Health Order requiring masks for those who are vaccinated. He noted that if the
 Council has interest, and in consultation with the City Attorney, the Council may consider
 signing such a letter this evening or choose to agendize it for a future meeting.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN TO:

  AGENDIZE THE CONSIDERATION OF AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO
  SIGN A LETTER TO THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY BOARD OF
  SUPERVISORS REGARDING AN EXEMPTION OF THE MASK MANDATE
  FOR THE PENINSULA CITIES.

 Discussion ensued regarding recent changes made today to the CDC guidelines,
 recommending masking in indoor public settings, regardless of vaccination status.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis reported that the City has received a request to appeal Planning
Commission approval PA-210169, which is tentatively scheduled for the Council’s
consideration on September 14.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JULY 27, 2021
 11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that she attended the June Equestrian Committee
meeting where the Committee encouraged the equestrian community to attend the Mayor’s
Ride in July, which was a huge success.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that she attended the Neighborhood Watch Meeting
at the end of June, where recent improvement in crime rates and an increase in coyote
sightings were discussed.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that she was nominated for the State Board of
Directors for the League of California Cities.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN attended the most recent South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) meeting, and stated that he will begin forwarding the highlight summaries from
these meetings to the entire Council. He stated that the SBCCOG is also scheduling a strategic
planning session in the near future, and invited input from the Council. COUNCIL MEMBER
HUFF added that the SBCCOG approved unanimously to hold a Town Hall at the Torrance
Cultural Center to discuss SB9 and SB10 legislation.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  LETTER TO CALIFORNIA CITIZENS REDISTRICTING COMMISSION

City Manager Grammer provided a brief staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved to:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE ATTACHED LETTER TO THE
  CALIFORNIA CITIZENS REDISTRICTING COMMISSION DESCRIBING THE
  PENINSULA  COMMUNITY’S  PREFERENCES  FOR  REGIONAL
  REPRESENTATION ALONGSIDE THE NORTHERLY SOUTH BAY CITIES.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.
